review.method: acceptance suite run locally with the retail capability; this harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, and the production index reader, sound reader, WAVE header reader and block decoder over every compressed member of both retail sound archives (zbd-adpcm-decode.json); when CS_FFMPEG names an ffmpeg binary it also compares production decodes with that independent implementation of the same two documented formats sample for sample; validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass. The independent cross-check ran: ffmpeg version 8.1.1 Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers decoded one member of each of the 7 distinct retail shapes (6091417 samples in total) and every sample equalled the production decode. The decode is a checked format claim, not a claim about how the original executable played the sound. Unresolved issues are recorded in the task's finding document (docs/findings/2026-10-02-t444-ima-and-ms-adpcm-block-decoding.md, section "Unusual and unobserved cases, recorded as found") and are restated here, one per item:"multi-channel IMA ADPCM, and MS ADPCM beyond two channels [status: unknown; why: no retail member declares them and the layouts documented for wider blocks differ, so they are refused rather than read; affected content: 0 retail members]" "what the original executable does with the decoded samples: pitch, volume, spatialisation, and whether it loops a sound [status: unknown; why: decided outside these bytes; no retail WAVE header declares a loop region; affected content: every sound member; feature F41]" "a trailing short block [status: not observed in retail; why: every retail `data` payload is a whole number of `nBlockAlign` blocks, so the sample count of a short final block follows the documented geometry and is covered by synthetic tests only; affected content: 0 retail members]" "whether the `cs_assets` consumer (which still calls stage F06-C's `SampleFormat::from_header`) reports these members as decoded [status: known gap, filed as a follow-up task; why: switching that consumer changes its F06-C `SoundReadiness::UnsupportedFormat` contract and is outside this task's owner paths; affected content: every sound member at runtime]"
